title: Reassembly: To fix a streaming reassembly bug, remove layer if all the data needs to be reassembled after calling a dissector
description:
## Description

During the first pass, the helper function reassemble_streaming_data_and_call_subdissector() will call subdissector several times, but the second pass will call subdissector fewer times than the first pass. If the pinfo->curr_layer_num was always added without regard to reassembly, reassembly will fail in the second or subsequent pass because the reassembly related functions, such as fragment_add(), process_reassembled_data() and get_virtual_frame_num64(), require the pinfo->curr_layer_num to be the same for the first and second or subsequent pass.

In old version of packet.c code, the newly added layer would only be removed when the subdissector returned 0. In this MR, the newly added layer would also be removed if it indicates that the data needs to be reassembled and dissected in the further according to the pinfo->desegment_offset/desegment_len attributes.

Before this MR, the subdissector avoid this issue by returning the length it handled (including return 0 if all the data must reassembled in the future). But this method is not compatible with the TCP reassembly mechanism by using pinfo->desegment_offset/desegment_len.

## Test Case

You can try this capture files [proto_a_proto_b_udp_tcp_reassembly_sample_case1.pcapng](/wireshark/wireshark/uploads/17038be9bc6df121fe4f5428d044e9b0/proto_a_proto_b_udp_tcp_reassembly_sample_case1.pcapng), [proto_a_proto_b_udp_tcp_reassembly_sample_case2.pcapng](/wireshark/wireshark/uploads/76621523e788431bd10bdc943eed12ad/proto_a_proto_b_udp_tcp_reassembly_sample_case2.pcapng), or 
[proto_a_proto_b_udp_tcp_reassembly_sample_case3.pcapng](/wireshark/wireshark/uploads/81860455ddb6be1ca1a97f78d8706c00/proto_a_proto_b_udp_tcp_reassembly_sample_case3.pcapng) from !10949 with plugin code [streaming_reassembly_proto_a_proto_b_source.tar.gz](/uploads/e9787811e59eb898b0f164f3fff8bc6c/streaming_reassembly_proto_a_proto_b_source.tar.gz) (upgraded).

notes.body: changed title from **Reassembly: {-R-}emove layer {-when-} the data {-of tvb was unhandled due-} to reassembl{-y for fixing a reassembly bug-}** to **Reassembly: {+To fix a streaming reassembly bug, r+}emove layer {+if all+} the data {+needs+} to {+be +}reassembl{+ed after calling a dissector+}**

I think that this approach is largely correct, as I thought about doing something similar in !6349 but this is more general.

If there is a tree but `saved_tree_count != tree->tree_data->count` and yet we want to remove the layer, that is arguably a bug by the subdirector (and also means different dissection next pass.) Not sure if we want to warn for it.

(As a side note, the reassembly and other problems can be somewhat reduced, though not eliminated, by using the newer "layer number of this particular protocol" value instead.)

When I first saw the pinfo->curr_layer_num, I thought its value represented the absolute layer number, and its behavior should be as: (add one before calling subdissector and subtract one after calling, regardless of whether the subdissector processed the data)

```
                              +-------------+
call subsubdissectors         |    ln==2    |
                         +----+(ln++)-(ln--)+----+       +------------------+
Call subdissectors:      |    ln==1      ln==1   |       |      ln==1       |
                 +-------+(ln++)-----------(ln--)+-------+(ln++)------(ln--)+------+
Call dissector:  | ln==0                           ln==0                     ln==0 |
                 +-----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

But in fact, normally its behavior seems to be like this:

```
                              +-------------+
call subsubdissectors         |      ln==2  |
                         +----+(ln++)-------+----+       +------------------+
Call subdissectors:      |    ln==1        ln==2 |       |      ln==3       |
                 +-------+(ln++)-----------------+-------+(ln++)------------+------+
Call dissector:  | ln==0                           ln==2                     ln==3 |
                 +-----------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Is it possible to modify the curr_layer_num or add a new abs_layer_num to behave in "absolute layer number" way mentioned previously for reassembly?

That could be useful for distinguishing tunneling from multiple PDUs at the same layer, but I don't think it could completely replace the current value without changes in a number of dissectors.

There's a number of dissectors that use `p_add_proto_data` with the current layer number, and that wouldn't work if multiple PDUs / dissector calls have the same layer number set.

It's possible that a combination of the new `curr_proto_layer_num` and the depth number you suggest could between themselves cover everything.

It seems a little complicated to me, I did not investigate purpose of curr_proto_layer_num yet. 😅

Will you continue to process this MR?

Here's another example of a file that has issues with the current proto layer being unstable: [http2-sample-dsb.pcapng](/uploads/9d1b7e4c917a6ecba20726962322da8e/http2-sample-dsb.pcapng)

In packet 182, the reassembled data is not displayed because of all the segmented TCP, fragmented TLS records, and HTTP/2 segments meaning that the layer numbers are different after the first pass.

For HTTP/2 with the "reassemble only at the end of the stream" method as there, it would be possible to as a workaround implement a local version of `process_reassembled_data` that doesn't use the layer number, since we know exactly when we want to retrieve the reassembled data (the END STREAM flag is set) as opposed to a FT_FRAMENUM link to the data.
Will this change be merged? Or what is the plan to fix this issue?

@AndersBroman Are you asking me?

I think my original idea was correct, and I do intend to apply this MR. However, I’m not entirely sure if this is the best solution.
@johnthacker Or is there a better solution than this one?

commits_data.message:
Reassembly: Remove layer when the data unhandled due to reassembly

The reassemble_streaming_data_and_call_subdissector() will call
subdissector many times during first pass, if the curr_layer_num
was always added without regard to reassembly, reassembly will
fail in the second pass. Now remove layer according to
pinfo->desegment_offset/desegment_len.
